definitions.explanation: An African wild horse with distinctive black and white striped coat.

examples.japanese: {縞馬|しまうま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{縞|しま}→縞：27905_shima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一頭|いっとう}⟦ずつ→〜ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{違|ちが}います→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Each zebra has a unique stripe pattern.

examples.japanese: ⟦サバンナ→サバンナ：28719_sabanna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{縞馬|しまうま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{群|む}れ→群れ：00298_mure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}ました→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: We saw a herd of zebras on the savanna.

examples.japanese: {縞馬|しまうま}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{似|に}て→似る：01159_niru⟧⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{別|べつ}→別：01216_betsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Zebras look like horses but are different animals.

examples.japanese: {縞馬|しまうま}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦アフリカ→アフリカ：01767_afurika⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んで→住む：00673_sumu⟧⟦います→いる：00495_iru⟧。

examples.english: The black and white stripes of zebras are said to help protect them from predators like lions.

notes:
Literally 'striped horse' (⟦{縞|しま}→縞：27905_shima⟧ 'stripe' + ⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧ 'horse'). In modern writing it is usually spelled in katakana, シマウマ; the kanji spelling is rare.

COUNTING PATTERNS:
- {一頭|いっとう}, {二頭|にとう}: zebras, like other large animals, are counted with ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧
